message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key traffic laws and regulations that apply in Texas, along with where you can find the full legal text and additional resources.

---

## 1. Governing Authority  
**Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – administers driver licensing, vehicle registration, and enforcement of the Texas Transportation Code.  
**Texas Transportation Code** – the statutory framework that governs all traffic rules, penalties, and administrative procedures in the state.

---

## 2. Major Traffic Law Areas

| Area | Key Statutes / Sections | Typical Penalties |
|------|------------------------|-------------------|
| **Speed Limits** | §545.001–545.004 | Fines, points, possible license suspension |
| **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat** | §545.021–545.023 | $50–$200 fine, points |
| **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | §545.051–545.053 | Fines up to $5,000, license revocation, jail |
| **Texting/Phone Use** | §545.061 | $50 fine, points |
| **Reckless Driving** | §545.041 | $500–$5,000 fine, license suspension |
| **Pedestrian & Bicycle** | §545.031 | $100–$1,000 fine, points |
| **Traffic Signal Violations** | §545.011 | $50–$200 fine, points |
| **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | §545.001 (registration), §545.001 (inspection) | Fines, vehicle impoundment |
| **Commercial Vehicle Regulations** | §545.001 (commercial), §545.001 (DOT) | Higher fines, stricter licensing |

> **Tip:** For the most up‑to‑date penalties, check the Texas DPS “Fine Schedule” online or the Texas Transportation Code’s “Schedule of Penalties” (Section 545.001).

---

## 3. How to Find the Full Text

| Resource | What It Offers | How to Access |
|----------|----------------|---------------|
| **Texas Transportation Code** | Complete statutory text | https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/ |
| **Texas DPS Fine Schedule** | Current fines for each offense | https://www.dps.texas.gov/ |
| **Texas DPS Driver Handbook** | Practical guide for drivers | https://www.dps.texas.gov/ |
| **Texas Legislature Online** | Bill history, amendments | https://capitol.texas.gov/ |
| **Texas Courts** | Case law interpreting statutes | https://www.txcourts.gov/ |

---

## 4. Common Enforcement Practices

| Practice | What It Means | Why It Matters |
|----------|---------------|----------------|
| **Points System** | Accumulating points on your license can lead to suspension | Points are tracked by the DPS; 12 points in 36 months triggers suspension |
| **Electronic Toll Collection** | TxTag, EZ Tag, etc. | Required for toll roads; failure to pay can result in fines |
| **Vehicle Inspection Stations** | Annual safety inspection | Failure to pass can lead to impoundment |
| **Roadside Checks** | Random checks for DUI, seat‑belt compliance | Helps enforce compliance and reduce accidents |

---

## 5. Resources for Specific Questions

| Question | Where to Look |
|----------|---------------|
| *What are the exact speed limits for different road types?* | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 |
| *How many points does a DUI carry?* | Texas DPS Fine Schedule |
| *What are the penalties for texting while driving?* | Texas Transportation Code §545.061 |
| *Where can I find the latest updates to the Texas Transportation Code?* | Texas Legislature Online, “Bill Tracker” |
| *How do I appeal a traffic ticket?* | Texas Courts “Traffic Ticket Appeals” page |

---

## 6. Quick Reference Cheat Sheet

| Offense | Fine | Points | Notes |
|---------|------|--------|-------|
| Speeding (up to 20 mph over limit) | $50–$200 | 1–2 | |
| Speeding (over 20 mph) | $200–$500 | 3–4 | |
| Seat‑belt (adult) | $50–$200 | 1 | |
| Seat‑belt (child) | $50–$200 | 1 | |
| DUI (first offense) | $500–$5,000 | 4–6 | License revocation |
| Texting while driving | $50 | 1 | |
| Reckless driving | $500–$5,000 | 4–6 | |
| Pedestrian violation | $100–$1,000 | 1–2 | |

> **Note:** These figures are approximate; always verify with the DPS Fine Schedule for the current year.

---

### Final Thought

If you need deeper legal analysis—such as how a specific case law has interpreted a section of the Texas Transportation Code—you can use the **lawsuit_search** function to locate relevant cases. Just let me know the topic and location, and I’ll fetch the latest litigation data for you.
